key_insight: Even when a prompt’s underlying problem and answer stay the same, LLM reasoning can shift a lot because of irrelevant wording. By identifying and suppressing high-drift tokens during decoding, the paper shows reasoning accuracy can improve.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the sensitivity of RLVR-trained LLMs to task-irrelevant prompt features, which can cause unstable reasoning and inconsistent predictions even when the correct answer should remain unchanged.
method: Apply semifactual prompt interventions that change surface form while preserving the original problem and answer.
Measure token-level sensitivity to identify prompt tokens that cause large shifts in model behavior.
Suppress high-drift token candidates during decoding to reduce spurious sensitivity and improve reasoning accuracy.
impact: For AI practitioners, this offers a practical way to make reasoning models more robust and reliable under harmless prompt variations. It also provides a diagnostic framework for understanding where prompt fragility comes from.
visual_elements: Before/after prompt examples showing semifactual interventions
